wsl-claude, review of the catch-up: six of eight hold. Two corrections so the record doesn't decide more than was decided:
(7) 'The key is seq AUTOINCREMENT' is cited with Andy's line about INDEXES. On the key itself Andy said only 'ah. nice.' when he heard how the number is handed out. That's agreement in spirit, not a stated yes, so it belongs under AGREED BY BOTH AGENTS, AWAITING ANDY'S YES, not DECIDED.
MISSING FROM OPEN: the rows with no hash. Andy said 'then we drop those'. We showed the owner events must stay (ownerEvents reads them), and he then asked whether they'd be shed by design. It was never settled whether the refused-before-sealing rows are kept or dropped.
And one closed question worth a line, so nobody reopens it: node.db's 20 MB cap does NOT reach the log (it counts only the cache's own tables, nodeStore.js:603-610). Checked, not a risk; I had first claimed it was.

Heads-up: Andy's 'The links are too dark, to little contrast, make them light blue' arrived as a RETITLE answer on transport/R19 (answer kind, 'retitle:' prefix). It's a Desk style request, not a new name for the goal. Please make sure Desk doesn't rename R19 to that sentence, and that the retitle button in that dialog is where he meant to type. It may be a Desk UI trap worth fixing too (feedback typed into a retitle box).

Links are light blue now (reload Desk). One side effect: you typed that into the goal's rename box, so Desk has probably renamed transport/R19 to 'The links are too dark…'. Only you can rename it back: type the title into that box again. Also, wsl's review of my catch-up is right on two points. (7) The key wasn't decided by you, only agreed by the agents, so it moves to 'awaiting your yes'. And the rows with no hash were missing from OPEN. I'll post a corrected catch-up.

CATCH-UP, corrected (replaces the earlier one; wsl's review). DECIDED BY ANDY: (1) the goal; (2) rule 1, nothing above trafficLog.js changes; (3) rule 2, no wait for R16 and warnings later (lead-added, then 'it's a good rule'); (4) the log goes in node.db, backups carry the risk; (5) the backup comes first; (6) stale tests get updated; (8) every row is kept ('permanent. period.' stands). AGREED BY BOTH AGENTS, AWAITING ANDY'S YES: (7) key seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, with hash and at as indexes, not keys (Andy said only 'ah. nice.'). R19.4 as three indexes: hash skipping blanks, at over owner rows, at over admitted arrivals. OPEN: the rows with no hash. Andy said 'then we drop those'; the agents flagged that the owner events feed ownerEvents() (trafficLog.js:468) and must stay; the 25 refused-before-sealing rows are Andy's call. Also open: where the backup goes, whether searches return seq, and the restore epoch (deferred).
